title: Group the graph by repo/workspace like Orca
description: Group coordinators, runs and loose terminals by the repo/workspace they act on (Orca's project grouping: repo of the worktree path, e.g. ~/orca/workspaces/<repo>/..., or the repo root name for non-Orca paths). Graph: each repo is a labelled translucent region (hull or rounded rect behind its nodes) holding its run clusters and its own loose terminals (no more single global loose group); repo regions arranged around the Queen; layout forces keep a repo's clusters together and regions apart. Sidebar: runs and loose terminals listed under collapsible repo headers with counts, like Orca's sidebar. Repo name in tooltips and the terminal panel header. Filters/search/keyboard order follow the grouping (J/K next run stays; add next/previous repo).
acceptance_criteria: Layout tests: nodes of a repo share a region, regions don't overlap, clusters stay distinct inside; sidebar grouping tests; persisted layout still restores.

title: Attendant shown as the run's coordinator
description: Orca's run.coordinator_handle is whichever terminal ran run-create, and the playbook has the attendant do that. Live: run_7c25cdcf46e0's coordinator_handle is term_df9f (title 'cp-wave-0923-ATTENDANT brief'); all 58 tasks were created by term_440d (now gone); Karl's current coordinator is elsewhere. Fix: NodeKind::Attendant. Identify the attendant: the declared handle when its title mentions 'attendant', or when other live terminals created the run's tasks / answer on its bus, or when its Claude transcript shows 'orca terminal send --terminal <h>' forwards. Identify the real coordinator as the most recent live of: the attendant's forward target (parse the attendant's session transcript via the claude session mapping, newest 'terminal send --terminal <h>' / '--terminal=<h>'), task creators (created_by_terminal_handle), bus senders for the run that are neither workers nor the attendant. Graph: Queen → coordinator; coordinator → attendant (small node, own shape, EdgeKind::Attendant) → workers stay on the coordinator. If no live coordinator: show the attendant with a 'coordinator gone' marker and link the Queen to the attendant. Whip, close, broadcast and the control API/MCP use the real coordinator (update FleetData::effective_coordinator accordingly).
acceptance_criteria: Model tests for each identification signal and the no-coordinator case; live check on run_7c25 lists attendant and coordinator correctly.

title: Manual whip: nudge agents now
description: Whip specific agents immediately, bypassing threshold and cooldown: 'Whip' button in the terminal panel header, 'Whip' in the node context menu (acts on the multi-selection), the multi-selection panel, key 'w'. Sends the standard Myrstack nudge (worker: heartbeat/continue; coordinator: act on the board/holding) via the same routing and sender as the automatic whip. 'Whip all stalled now' button (Queen panel + whip settings window) runs an immediate full whip pass. Manual whips are live even when the automatic whip is in dry-run (explicit user action). NeedsInput targets get a warning in a small confirm popover (nudge won't answer the prompt). Queen/subagents/dead terminals are skipped with a reason. Results go to the whip log (marked manual) and inline. Control API method 'whip' (ids | stalled:true) and MCP tool 'whip_agents' (destructive).
acceptance_criteria: Tests: manual plan per node kind, skip reasons, bypasses cooldown but records the nudge for echo suppression and the ladder, dry-run doesn't block manual, log entries marked manual, key/menu/API mapping; nothing sent to real agents in testing.

title: Built-in fleet chat pane
description: A chat pane inside the Myrstack window backed by a Claude Code session that Myrstack spawns at startup and owns (not an Orca terminal, so never in the graph). Used to control the fleet and ask for insights. Spawn 'claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --verbose --include-partial-messages --permission-prompts host' with the myrstack MCP server, an appended system prompt (fleet-control role; load the coordinator playbook via the myrstack MCP), cwd in the app data dir. Myrstack answers permission prompts through the stream-json control protocol with an in-pane Approve/Deny card. Render streaming assistant text as markdown, tool calls as collapsible rows, errors inline. Resume the last session on restart, 'New chat' button, stop/interrupt button, model shown. Pane toggles with a hotkey and a top-bar button; coexists with the node panels.
acceptance_criteria: Protocol handling tested against recorded stream-json fixtures (text deltas, tool_use/tool_result, permission control requests, result, errors); process lifecycle (spawn, restart, resume, kill on exit) tested with a fake claude script; live smoke: one read-only question answered in the pane using fleet_status.

title: Serve the playbook via MCP prompts, tools and CLI
description: Read playbook/ from disk on every request (dir: MYRSTACK_PLAYBOOK_DIR, else the repo path baked in at build time via CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/playbook, else ~/Documents/agents). MCP prompts (slash commands in Claude Code): coordinator, attendant, worker — each returns the role's document(s). MCP tools: get_playbook(role|file, section?) returning a whole doc or one '## ' section; list_playbook. MCP resources for each file (myrstack://playbook/<file>). CLI: 'myrstack playbook <role|file> [--section X]'. Every response carries a version stamp: the git commit + dirty flag of playbook/ (git -C <dir> log -1 --format=%h -- playbook; plus a content hash) so readers can tell which version they got. Works without the app running (served by the mcp process itself).
acceptance_criteria: Tests with a temp playbook dir: prompts/list + prompts/get, tools, resources/list + resources/read, section extraction, missing file errors, version stamp; live: 'myrstack playbook coordinator' prints the playbook.

title: M7: Myrstack owns the fleet playbook
description: Playbook, protocol and templates live in playbook/ (git) and are served by Myrstack so agents fetch their rules instead of reading a path.

title: Signed broadcasts agents can verify
description: Agents refuse Myrstack broadcasts because anyone can claim --from myrstack-karl (observed: a worker refused a broadcast to clean up failed agents and flagged it as unverified). Sign every broadcast (and whip nudge) with an HMAC-SHA256 over (orca message id if known, else a nonce, run id, subject, body) using a random key generated on first use at <data dir>/signing.key (0600). Append a footer to the message body: '— Karl via Myrstack (<origin: dashboard|chat>) · verify: myrstack verify <msg-ref> <sig>'. Keep a sent-log (<data dir>/sent.jsonl: msg-ref, time, origin, run, body hash, sig). 'myrstack verify <msg-ref> <sig>' prints VERIFIED with sender, time and origin when the signature matches and the bus message's current text (read via orca orchestration inbox) hashes to the logged value; NOT VERIFIED otherwise; exit code 0/1. Origin 'chat' marks sends that came through the control API/MCP. Whip nudges use a distinct footer ('Myrstack whip, liveness ping, no authority') and verify as such.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests: sign/verify round trip, tampered body fails, copied signature on another message fails, unknown ref fails, origin shown; key created with 0600; docs/heartbeat-convention.md and docs/playbook-proposal addendum describe the rule; no real messages sent in testing.
close_reason: Dropped: Karl prefers a plain trust rule for Queen broadcasts (no signing)

title: Box-select nodes with left-drag; pan with right-drag; bulk close
description: Left-drag on empty graph space draws a selection rectangle and selects every node inside it (Shift/Cmd adds to the selection; Shift/Cmd-click toggles a single node). Left-drag on a node still moves the node. Right-drag pans the view (instead of left-drag); a right-click without dragging still opens the node context menu. With several nodes selected: highlight them all, the right panel shows an 'N selected' panel listing them with a 'Close N sessions…' button, Delete/Backspace/x and the context menu ('Close N selected…') open the close dialog for all of them (bulk plan; Queen/subagents skipped with a note). Esc clears the multi-selection. Single-click keeps today's behaviour (select one, open its panel).
acceptance_criteria: Headless egui tests simulating pointer input: rectangle selects the right nodes, modifier adds, node drag moves not selects, right-drag pans, right-click menu still works; key commands on a multi-selection open a bulk close; quality gate passes.

title: Queen node: central hub linked to every coordinator
description: Add a central 'Queen' node (NodeKind::Queen, one per snapshot, stable id 'queen') at the center of the graph, with an edge (EdgeKind::Queen) to every coordinator and every loose terminal so the whole fleet reads as one connected colony. Layout: queen anchored at the view center; run clusters arranged around it (queen edges must not pull clusters into a knot — use a weak/long spring or exclude queen edges from the cluster forces and add a radial arrangement). Styling: distinct shape (e.g. hexagon or crown), larger, neutral/gold color, state = worst state of the fleet (NeedsInput if any node needs input, Stalled if any escalation), faint thin queen edges. Selecting the queen opens a Queen panel in the right panel: fleet summary (counts by state, runs, needs-input list with click-to-select, whip status, quotas) and the broadcast composer (move/reuse the existing broadcast window's UI there; keep the top-bar Broadcast button opening the queen panel). Excluded from close/kill, search results show it, keyboard nav starts at it.
acceptance_criteria: Queen appears centered with edges to all coordinators and loose terminals; clusters still distinct (layout tests updated); queen panel shows summary and broadcasts (tested with fakes, nothing sent).

title: Local control API in the app
description: While Myrstack runs, serve a local control API so other processes (the MCP server) can query and drive it. Unix socket in the app data dir (0600) or 127.0.0.1 with a token file. Reads come from a shared status view the app updates on each snapshot rebuild: fleet summary (runs, coordinators, workers, loose terminals, subagents with state, idle time, NeedsInput prompt, stall/escalation, tokens), whip status + recent log, quotas, alerts. Actions go through the app's existing paths via a command channel polled in logic(): send text/Enter/Esc/interrupt to a terminal, close/kill (after the close bead lands), broadcast, whip settings (enable, dry-run), and dashboard control: select/focus node, set filter, switch view, fit. Versioned JSON protocol documented in docs/control-api.md.
acceptance_criteria: Integration test: start the server on a temp socket against a fake app state, exercise every read and action; app runs with the server enabled and responds to a status request.

title: MCP server: myrstack mcp
description: 'myrstack mcp' subcommand speaking MCP over stdio that proxies to the running app's control API. Tools: fleet_status (summary + counts), list_agents (filters: state, run, repo, kind), get_agent (details + current screen tail), send_to_agent (text / enter / esc / interrupt), close_agent, broadcast_to_coordinators, whip_status, set_whip (enabled/dry_run), focus_agent / set_filter / set_view (dashboard control), alerts. Mark mutating tools with destructiveHint so the chat client asks first. Clear error when Myrstack isn't running; consider a read-only headless fallback for fleet_status using the orca client directly.
acceptance_criteria: Protocol tests (initialize, tools/list, tools/call) against a fake control API; a live smoke run: initialize + tools/list + fleet_status against the running app.

title: Close and kill sessions
description: Close a selected terminal session from Myrstack: button in the terminal panel header, node context menu, and a keyboard shortcut, each behind a confirmation. Workers with an active dispatch: 'orca orchestration worker-stop --dispatch <id>' first (fences the dispatch so orchestration state stays consistent), then 'orca terminal close --terminal <h>' (option: whole tab with --tab). Coordinators: warn that the run loses its coordinator. Loose terminals: close directly. Subagents: not closable (in-process) — disabled with a tooltip. Bulk: close a set (e.g. all nodes currently shown by the sidebar filter, or multi-selected nodes) behind a confirmation listing every target. Runs on the ActionRunner thread; results shown inline and in an action log.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests with fakes for action planning (worker-stop then close, coordinator warning, subagent refusal, bulk plan); manual steps for Karl; never closes a real terminal during development.

title: Whip: skip abandoned runs and set an explicit sender
description: From the live dry-run: (1) it would nudge the coordinator of run_b76b8ed07bb1 idle for 719h (finished task with no follow-up) — CoordinatorIdle/UnansweredAsk must skip runs with no activity (run updated_at, coordinator output, bus messages) for > 24 h, like QuietNoTasks already does; make the abandon window a setting. (2) Sender attribution: without --from and without ORCA_* identity env, orca orchestration send falls back to terminal.resolveActive (the focused terminal) — see Orca CLI handlers/orchestration/terminal-identity.js. Find an accepted --from value for an external sender (read the CLI source; don't send) and set OutgoingMessage.from for all whip and broadcast sends; if none exists, document it and send nudges via terminal send instead.
acceptance_criteria: Dry-run against the live fleet produces no nudges for runs idle > 24h; every whip/broadcast send has an explicit, documented sender.

title: Wire the whip into the app
description: Run WhipEngine tick+execute on a background thread every tick_ms using the latest FleetData (seed needs_input from NeedsInput nodes); OrcaExecutor live, DryRunExecutor when dry_run. Settings window (enabled, dry-run, threshold, cooldown, max nudges, notify) that loads/saves Settings. Escalated handles render as Stalled/red (StateInputs.stalled). Fix: output caused by our own nudge must not count as progress — ignore terminal output within ~60 s after a nudge to that terminal when computing progress. Set the sender env deliberately (unset ORCA_TERMINAL_HANDLE etc. for the whip's orca calls) so nudges aren't attributed to whatever Orca terminal launched Myrstack.
acceptance_criteria: Dry-run whip runs live in the app and its intended actions show in the log; toggling dry-run off is a single settings switch; tests for the nudge-echo fix.

title: Coordinator node can be the wrong terminal
description: In real data run.coordinator_handle (term_df9f…) differs from the terminal that creates the run's tasks and sends coordinator messages (term_440d…), likely after the coordinator re-bound with run-use from a new terminal. The model should pick the live coordinator: prefer coordinator_handle if live, else the most recent live created_by_terminal_handle of the run's tasks / sender of run-level messages. Found by myr-9zx.1.

title: Nudge actions, escalation and cooldown
description: `orchestration send` nudge from Myrstack asking for a heartbeat or to continue; fall back to `terminal send --enter` when idle at a prompt. Escalate nudge -> nudge -> notification; per-task cooldown.
acceptance_criteria: A paused worker is nudged once per cooldown and escalates after max nudges.
notes: Nudge text must start with 'Myrstack:' (docs/heartbeat-convention.md). Coordinators have no dispatch so can't send heartbeat; their progress is task-board activity or a 'holding: <reason>' status message.

title: Stall rules
description: Worker stalled: dispatched, no progress beyond the threshold, not NeedsInput. Coordinator stalled: ready or finished tasks with no coordinator activity. Taskless runs: coordinator lastOutputAt.
acceptance_criteria: Table-driven tests for each rule and the NeedsInput exemption.
notes: From myr-9zx.7: a worker blocked on an unanswered 'ask' question legitimately stops heartbeating — count that as a stalled coordinator, not a stalled worker. Orca also stores last_heartbeat_at per dispatch (dispatch-show). Heartbeats after worker_done are rejected; ignore them.

title: Progress tracker
description: Per task: last progress = newest of an owner bus message referring to the task (heartbeat payload.taskId), a status change, or the owner's lastOutputAt as fallback. Owner comes from worker-list taskId -> agentTerminalHandle.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests over fixture tasks, workers and inbox.

title: ~20% CPU while a NeedsInput node is visible
description: Release build, window visible, one real NeedsInput terminal on screen: frame_stats shows ~13 fps driven by the NeedsInput pulse (src/ui/graph/shape.rs:353), and ps shows ~21% CPU — i.e. ~15 ms CPU per frame. myr-hrw.6 measured ~1% only with no pulsing node. Two fixes: (1) make the NeedsInput attention cue cheap — lower pulse rate (e.g. 2-4 fps) or a static high-contrast badge after a few pulses, and repaint only the graph area if egui allows; (2) cut per-frame cost — profile with 'sample <pid> 5' (sidebar incl. the whip log's 100 rows and runs list, graph drawing of ~100 nodes with labels, tessellation) and cache/limit what's drawn (e.g. only lay out visible whip-log rows via ScrollArea::show_rows).
acceptance_criteria: Release build, window visible, with a NeedsInput node on screen: < 5% CPU; with none: ~1% as before. Report before/after with frame_stats fps.

title: Whip: abandon setting in UI; don't let reused coordinators revive old runs
description: Follow-ups from myr-9zx.9: (1) expose WhipSettings.abandon_after_ms in the settings window (hours). (2) Coordinator terminal output counts as run activity, so a coordinator terminal still open and busy with unrelated work keeps old runs alive (live: run_60927f57889a last updated 31 Aug and run_57c04fae0941 get nudged because their coordinators printed output in the last 2-3 h). Count coordinator output as run activity only while the run has open work it could be acting on, and treat a run as superseded when its coordinator terminal is the coordinator of a newer run (reuse the QuietNoTasks superseded check).
acceptance_criteria: Live dry-run: no nudges for runs whose coordinator has moved on to a newer run; abandon window editable in the settings window.

title: Idle CPU ~20% in release build
description: Release build with the live fleet (~47 terminals, 8 active runs) sits at 17-21% CPU 10-50 s after start with no interaction. Suspects: Working-node pulse animation repainting every 33 ms (many terminals are Working), per-second snapshot rebuild + graph sync, layout never pausing because sync keeps waking it, the Claude worker. Profile (e.g. samply / Instruments) and get idle below ~3%.
